title: Latency stitching workflow and exemplar traces
summary: Working notes documenting a practical workflow for stitching partial traces from edge proxies, batching workers, and model GPU workers into coherent end-to-end timelines. Includes exemplar traces across three cohorts (short prompt warm, long prompt warm, cold-start with KV miss), per-stage median/p95/p99 summaries, and prioritized action items.
methodology: We collected sampled traces from distributed collectors over a 72h window (2025-01-28 to 2025-01-30) across two hardware classes (A100 and H100 instances). Traces were pre-filtered by request id where available; where request id was missing we applied a heuristic: match on client-ip + unix-ts (±200ms) + route + user-id hash. Stitched spans keep original start/end timestamps and we annotate inferred boundaries with a confidence tag (high|medium|low). Quantiles computed on reconstructed per-request end-to-end duration using simple weighting by sampling rate. Batching events are captured as explicit spans (batch-enter, batch-wait, batch-execute). KV cache events include a kv-lookup span and a kv-miss span when applicable.
cohorts: short-prompt-warm: user prompts < 80 tokens, model warm (hot KV), representative QPS: 450
long-prompt-warm: user prompts 200-800 tokens, model warm, representative QPS: 120
cold-start-kv-miss: any prompt length, upstream KV miss triggered, representative QPS: 30
quantile_summary: Aggregated E2E latencies (ms) by cohort: short-prompt-warm p50=42ms, p95=110ms, p99=240ms; long-prompt-warm p50=180ms, p95=410ms, p99=920ms; cold-start-kv-miss p50=320ms, p95=760ms, p99=1600ms. Note: H100 runs ~15% lower median on long prompts, A100 slightly better in short prompt tail under heavy batching.
per_stage_breakdowns: short-prompt-warm breakdown (median/p95/p99 in ms): ingress-proxy 4/10/25; tokenization 2/5/12; routing+auth 3/9/20; batch-wait 10/40/110; model-exec 15/30/65; kv-check 2/6/18; egress-serialize 4/10/30; network-egress 2/4/8

long-prompt-warm breakdown (median/p95/p99 in ms): ingress-proxy 6/12/28; tokenization 8/22/48; routing+auth 5/14/26; batch-wait 30/90/220; model-exec 100/230/560; kv-check 4/12/35; egress-serialize 10/28/60; network-egress 7/18/40

cold-start-kv-miss breakdown (median/p95/p99 in ms): ingress-proxy 8/18/40; tokenization 6/16/36; routing+auth 6/15/34; batch-wait 40/140/380; kv-lookup 20/80/220 (miss path triggers remote-kv-populate + consistency checks); model-exec 140/340/760; egress-serialize 12/36/90; network-egress 12/28/70
representative_traces: trace-id: rwh-20250129-0001 (short warm) - total 53ms; notable: batch-wait 18ms spike due to synchronous flush at 10ms threshold, model-exec 20ms; confidence: high

trace-id: rwh-20250130-0222 (long warm) - total 612ms; notable: sustained model-exec 420ms, tokenization pipeline blocked by backpressure in tokenizer pool (~60ms wait), batch-wait 80ms; confidence: high

trace-id: rwh-20250128-1437 (cold kv miss) - total 1288ms; notable: kv-lookup miss 310ms including remote-populate, double-write consistency check 120ms, model warm-up microsecond-level cold pages 220ms; confidence: medium
notable_findings: Batch boundaries are the single largest contributor to p95/p99 tail for short prompts. There are periodic synchronous flushes triggered by a timer misconfiguration (10ms) which coincide with microbursts of p95s.

KV miss path amplifies tail because remote-populate is serialized and triggers additional consistency verification spans; cold-start traffic should be rate-limited to avoid cascading queuing in batcher threads.

Tokenizer pool starvation observed under mixed workloads: when >30% of QPS are long prompts tokenizer threads are saturated causing a head-of-line effect that increases p95 across short prompt cohort.
Hardware differences: H100 reduces model-exec median on long prompts but exhibits a slightly higher variance for small batches due to kernel scheduling contention in our current runtime.
A small fraction (~0.6%) of traces lacked request id and were stitched with low confidence heuristics; those have slightly higher apparent tail — likely an instrumentation timing skew.
next_steps: (P0) Adjust batcher timer from 10ms -> 4ms and add jitter; run 48h A/B against control and capture full trace set (owner: Arjun)
(P0) Implement async remote-kv-populate to decouple remote IO from batch execution path (owner: Lena)
(P1) Increase tokenizer pool autoscaling threshold and add backpressure signals to proxy to limit long-prompt concurrency (owner: Noah)
(P2) Add trace-level sampling tags that indicate confidence and stitch-method so downstream owners can filter low-confidence reconstructions
(P3) Run hardware comparison bench with synthetic load focused on small-batch microbursts to quantify H100 kernel scheduling variance
